notes:
Checked on 2026-10-09. Read all 404 lines of the supplied markdown conversion, covering the complete 10-page published article, end matter and references; no appendix is included or referenced. Verified the Data Availability Statement directly in PDF page index 8 (printed p. 9). The sole availability statement is 'Data available on request.' No data/code/materials repository, preregistration or supplementary-file availability statement is given for S1. The screening form's data_url repeats the on-request statement and contains no URL; code_url is empty.

No relevant research-data deposit was identified, so deposits is empty. The on_request status records the authors' statement, not a verified response to an access request. No authors were contacted, no account was used or created, and no access request was submitted. No participant-level data file was available to inspect; arm assignments, outcome columns, participant texts and analyzed row counts could not be confirmed.

Consequently the public material found does not resolve final.open_items concerning the number failing the attention check, per-arm analyzed DAT counts, missing DAT observations, or the valid-case/regression sample discrepancy. It does not provide the participant words needed for diversity measures or participant records for recomputing arm means, SDs or SEs. Table 2 (p. 4) prints the three prime lists, which are stimulus materials, not participants' responses; published aggregate statistics are not a participant dataset.

Publisher check: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jocb.70022 returned HTTP 403 and a 'Just a moment...' bot-check page. The DOI also resolved to that page and returned HTTP 403. No attempt was made to pass the bot check. Publisher supplementary-file availability therefore remains unverified. Confidence is medium because the on-request statement is explicit but the inaccessible publisher page prevents a complete supplementary-file check.

Fallback to the known institutional article copy: the University of Adelaide DSpace API returned HTTP 200 for bitstream 945f2449-ca13-432c-81a7-09b44078a813, its parent bundle, the parent item (7a86b545-9c1f-4852-9c34-04196b429a76; handle 11541.2/43662), the item's bundles and the ORIGINAL bundle's bitstreams. The item has one bundle and one file: the published article PDF, 352098 bytes. No separate data or supplemental file is listed. Its CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 rights apply to the article; no dataset license is confirmed. This article-only repository copy is not counted as a research-data deposit. File listing: https://digital.library.adelaide.edu.au/server/api/core/bundles/f6c46fec-b290-4e94-b65e-2f60e5f99d04/bitstreams ; bundle listing: https://digital.library.adelaide.edu.au/server/api/core/items/7a86b545-9c1f-4852-9c34-04196b429a76/bundles .

The OSF DOI in the p. 9 bibliography, https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/9wh2f, is a citation to Marmolejo-Ramos's work, not a deposit for c097. The preprint metadata endpoint https://api.osf.io/v2/preprints/9wh2f/ returned HTTP 200 and identified 'Factors Influencing Trust in Algorithmic Decision-Making: An Indirect Scenario-based Experiment', a different study of algorithmic trust. It was excluded. Other nonmatching search results were also excluded rather than represented as deposits for c097.

Initial Zenodo size=100 errors are retained with null result counts; successful size=25 requests supplied the usable results. Search absence is not proof that no unindexed or differently named deposit exists.
